Let me analyze this conflict.

Register applicant: "Tuna Tarti ve Elektronik Sistemler Ltd. Sti."
Document applicant: "Tuna Tartı ve Elektronik Sistemler Ltd. Sti."

The difference: "Tarti" vs "Tartı" — this is a Turkish dotted/dotless i difference (dotless ı vs dotted i). This is an accent/diacritic difference, which per the rules = same-entity. Best value: The document is the legal instrument, but the rules say "same-entity" — what should best_value be? The rules say for number/year format differences = same-entity with register's canonical form. For same-entity generally (spelling drift, accents), what's the best value? The document is the legal instrument, so best_value from document seems appropriate. Actually the rules only explicitly state best_value for document-noise (register), different-entity (document), and same-entity for number/year (register canonical form). For same-entity spelling/accent drift, the document is the legal instrument, so best_value = document's value: "Tuna Tartı ve Elektronik Sistemler Ltd. Sti."

The Turkish "Tartı" (with dotless ı) is the correct Turkish spelling for "scale/weighing". So the document value is the more accurate one. Verdict: same-entity, best_value from document.

One short sentence why: "Tarti vs Tartı is only a Turkish dotless-i diacritic drift naming the same company; the certificate document is the legal instrument, so keep its accented form."
